title: Parameter-sensitive risk functions (ACP-SPEC-001 §8.3, RK-2)
description:
Deterministic functions from a Proposal's parameters and its targets' effective tiers to a risk level.

RK-2 exists because static per-action risk is insufficient: `modify_firewall_rule = HIGH` says nothing useful, since risk is a function of PARAMETERS and TARGETS, not action names.

THE ABSENT CASE DIFFERS FROM floors AND reversibility. An action with no risk function is REFUSED at §8.4 step 3 — it is NOT graded HIGH. Refusing and grading-HIGH are different behaviours: grading HIGH would route an unknown action into the human quorum, which looks conservative but silently teaches approvers to rubber-stamp things the policy author never considered. P-4: unknown is never LOW, and here it is not HIGH either — it is a refusal.

TR-8: these functions are evaluated by the Executor over the INDEPENDENTLY RECEIVED canonical Proposal and the trusted bundle, ignoring every Context-Store raise and ignoring any risk value asserted in the receipt. The recomputed value is what all subsequent attestation requirements key on.

x-acp-absent.why: THE ABSENT CASE HERE IS NOT THE ABSENT CASE IN floors OR reversibility. An action with no risk function is REFUSED, not graded HIGH. Grading HIGH would route an unknown action into the human quorum, which looks conservative and is worse: it teaches approvers to rubber-stamp things the policy author never considered (T-26 habituation, AT-7). P-4 says unknown is never LOW; here it is not HIGH either. A lookup returning `Option` would let a caller reach for HIGH as the obvious safe default and get this exactly wrong.

applies_to.description: Action class this function grades. At most one function per action class — two functions for one class is an ambiguity, not a merge, and the loader refuses it.

raise_to.description: Clauses evaluated in order. MONOTONE BY CONSTRUCTION: a clause can only raise the level, never lower it, which is why the field is `raise_to` and there is no `lower_to`. Monotonicity is what makes the Dafny proof that floors dominate raises tractable — a lowering clause would let a crafted parameter walk a HIGH action down to LOW.

if.description:
An EL-1 expression. EL-1 is deliberately minimal, TOTAL (no expression can fail to evaluate, so there is no error path to fall open through) and monotone.

PRECEDENCE IS NORMATIVE: `&&` binds tighter than `||`. That sentence exists because its absence WAS a defect — Z1, found by building two evaluators from the prose alone and running 10,000 differential cases until they disagreed. An implementation that leaves precedence to its host language reproduces the ambiguity.

risk.description:
Ordered LOW < MEDIUM < HIGH. §8.4 composes with max.

A RISK LEVEL IS NOT A RESOURCE TIER. This is a different ladder from `floors.schema.json`'s T0..T3, over a different subject, and §8.4 composes both with max — which is exactly why one type served for both until someone looked. The Rust and TypeScript definitions carried a single `RiskTier` enum whose doc comment cited RK-1's absent-⇒-T3 rule and whose values were LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, so the fail-safe default was stated in the wrong domain in both. Generated separately, and named separately, for that reason.
